stories.title: Vulnerability management: The cybersecurity industry is still solving the wrong problem
stories.why: We have never been short of vulnerabilities. We have always struggled with remedial work. For decades, the cybersecurity industry has approached vulnerability management from the wrong end.

stories.title: AI unearths ‘internet breaker’ flaws in Nginx web server
stories.why: Nginx, the web server estimated to power a third of the internet, has shipped fixes for multiple vulnerabilities, including a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw that puts millions of websites at risk…

stories.title: How AI is changing the nature of cyberattacks
stories.why: AI may be helping cyberattackers increase the speed and scale of their operations, but it is not yet changing their core objectives or the techniques they employ as part of their attack chains.

stories.title: Indirect prompt injection via documents, email and RAG sources
stories.why: Indirect prompt injection is one of the more subtle risks in AI-enabled workflows because the malicious instruction is hidden inside content the system is meant to trust.

stories.title: Four Days Early: Why AI-Found Vulnerabilities Demand Protection That’s Already On
stories.why: In October 2026, attackers went after PHP2Shell four days before a fix existed. Nearly every WAF provider published a rule within about a day.

stories.title: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters
stories.why: Attackers are using deepfakes, helpdesk impersonation, and fake IT support requests to deceive employees and gain unauthorized access to corporate systems.
